speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; can you describe exactly how this rash on your scalp and forehead feels and when it first appeared? Have you noticed any itching, burning, or pain associated with it?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, thank you for that information. Does the rash appear greasy or yellowish in certain areas, and have the parents tried any specific creams or oils to treat it? Also, are there any signs of the rash spreading to the diaper area or behind the ears?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the greasy yellow scales and the distribution on the scalp and forehead, this appears to be infantile seborrheic dermatitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap)
